source_text: This should be considered in clinical trials of transmission-reducing candidate drugs and vaccines
evidence_reasoning: This is a recommendation for trial design based on the study findings.

claim: The highly overdispersed distribution of gametocytes in the host population and the non-linear relationship between gametocytes/asexual parasite density and mosquito infection means that the impact of different transmission-reducing interventions on overall transmission at the population level will be far from intuitive.
source_text: The highly overdispersed distribution of gametocytes in the host population and the non-linear relationship between gametocytes/asexual parasite density and mosquito infection means that the impact of different transmission-reducing interventions on overall transmission at the population level will be far from intuitive
evidence_reasoning: This combines observed patterns (overdispersion and non-linearity) with inference about their implications for intervention impact.

claim: QT-NASBA is routinely used to estimate pathogen density.
source_text: Quantitative nucleic acid sequence-based amplification (QT-NASBA) is routinely used to estimate pathogen density
evidence_reasoning: This describes the established use of the technique.

claim: Like all diagnostic methods, QT-NASBA is prone to measurement error.
source_text: Like all diagnostic methods, it is prone to measurement error
evidence_reasoning: This is a general principle about diagnostic methods.

claim: The QT-NASBA assay measures time to positivity (TTP), which is the time it takes for the number of target amplicons detected to exceed a defined threshold.
source_text: The assay measures time to positivity (TTP), which is the time it takes for the number of target amplicons detected to exceed a defined threshold
evidence_reasoning: This describes the technical basis of the method (Schneider et al., 2004).

claim: The relationship between TTP and gametocyte density is estimated by fitting a linear regression to TTP estimates generated using a sample with known gametocyte density.
source_text: The relationship between TTP and gametocyte density is estimated by fitting a linear regression to TTP estimates generated using a sample with known gametocyte density (a 10-fold dilution series of in vitro cultured gametocytes ranging from 106 to 101 gametocytes per millilitre)
evidence_reasoning: This describes the calibration method used in the study.

claim: Calibration lines can vary between runs and batches of reagents.
source_text: Calibration lines can vary between runs and batches of reagents
evidence_reasoning: This reflects practical knowledge about assay variability.

claim: The accuracy of gametocyte density estimates can be improved by running multiple assays on the same sample and then taking the mean of all the estimates.
source_text: The accuracy of gametocyte density estimates can also be improved by running multiple assays on the same sample and then taking the mean of all the ln x′ estimates
evidence_reasoning: This is a standard statistical principle for reducing measurement error.

claim: In the Burkina Faso dataset, an average of 2.63 assays per unknown blood sample were carried out.
source_text: In the Burkina Faso dataset, multiple assays were carried out on the same blood sample (an average of 2.63 assays per unknown blood sample)
evidence_reasoning: This describes a feature of the data collection protocol.

claim: Plasmodium falciparum–infected blood was collected from children and fed through a membrane to A. gambiae sensu stricto mosquitoes that were dissected 7–9 days later to determine infection (oocyst carriage).
source_text: Plasmodium falciparum–infected blood was collected from children and fed through a membrane to A. gambiae sensu stricto mosquitoes that were dissected 7–9 days later to determine infection (oocyst carriage)
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental protocol.

claim: Data from 171 mosquito feeds on patients' blood conducted in Burkina Faso and Kenya were combined and used to fit a quantitative relationship between gametocyte density, asexual parasite density, host age, and mosquito infection.
source_text: Data from 171 mosquito feeds on patients' blood conducted in Burkina Faso (Ouédraogo et al., 2009) and Kenya (Schneider et al., 2007) were combined and used to fit a quantitative relationship between gametocyte density, asexual parasite density, host age, and mosquito infection (proportion of mosquitoes developing oocysts)
evidence_reasoning: This describes the data sources and analytical approach.

claim: The uncertainty in gametocyte density estimates (the intra-assay variability) was quantified by fitting a hierarchical model to 16 independent dilution series.
source_text: Gametocyte density was quantified using QT-NASBA, and the uncertainty in the density estimates (the intra-assay variability) was quantified by fitting a hierarchical model to the 16 independent dilution series
evidence_reasoning: This describes the statistical method for quantifying measurement uncertainty.

claim: The precise shape of the relationship between gametocyte density and mosquito infection was determined by fitting a range of different functional forms and statistically determining which gave the best fit.
source_text: The precise shape of the relationship was determined by fitting a range of different functional forms (a modified constant, linear, power, hyperbolic, sigmoid, and Gompertz functions) to data presented in Figure 1—source data 1 and statistically determining which gave the best fit
evidence_reasoning: This describes the model selection approach.

claim: Asexual parasite density was categorized as being either undetectable, low (<1000 parasites per microlitre of blood), or high (≥1000 parasites per microlitre of blood).
source_text: Asexual parasite density (estimated by microscopy) was categorized as being either undetectable (z1 = 0), low (<1000 parasites per microlitre of blood, z1 = 1) or high (≥1000 parasites per microlitre of blood, z1 = 2)
evidence_reasoning: This describes how a variable was coded in the analysis.

claim: Hosts were classified into two different age categories: <6 years (children) or ≥6 years (older children).
source_text: Hosts were classified into two different age categories (<6 years [children, z2 = 0] or ≥ 6 yr [older children, z2 = 1)
evidence_reasoning: This describes how age was categorized in the analysis.

claim: Mosquito infection was allowed to vary between Burkina Faso and Kenya in the model.
source_text: Mosquito infection was allowed to vary between Burkina Faso and Kenya (z3 = 0 for Burkina Faso, z3 = 1 for Kenya)
evidence_reasoning: This describes a feature of the statistical model.

claim: Evidence indicates that transmission is possible even at very low gametocyte densities.
source_text: Evidence indicates that transmission is possible even at very low gametocyte densities
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by references to Schneider et al., 2007; Ouédraogo et al., 2009.

claim: To investigate whether mosquito infection is best predicted by gametocyte density on the arithmetic or logarithmic scale, both hypotheses were tested in the model and model fits were compared.
source_text: To investigate whether mosquito infection is best predicted by gametocyte density on the arithmetic or logarithmic scale, both hypotheses were tested in the model, substituting an estimate of gametocyte density on the logarithmic scale (lnx′^) for x^′ in equations 3 and 4 and comparing model fits
evidence_reasoning: This describes a model comparison performed in the analysis.

claim: The model quantifying the uncertainty in gametocyte density estimates was fitted at the same time as the regression determining the relationship between gametocyte density and the proportion of mosquitoes infected using Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods.
source_text: The model quantifying the uncertainty in gametocyte density estimates was fitted at the same time as the regression determining the relationship between gametocyte density (and other covariates) and the proportion of mosquitoes infected using Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods
evidence_reasoning: This describes the statistical fitting procedure.

claim: Fitting the models simultaneously enables the uncertainty in the gametocyte density estimates to be reflected in the uncertainty of the shape of the relationship.
source_text: Fitting the models simultaneously enables the uncertainty in the gametocyte density estimates to be reflected in the uncertainty of the shape of the relationship
evidence_reasoning: This explains the rationale for the simultaneous fitting approach.

claim: Blood samples were randomly collected from 412 hosts from a single village in Burkina Faso.
source_text: Blood samples were randomly collected from 412 hosts from a single village in Burkina Faso
evidence_reasoning: This describes the sampling design for the cross-sectional survey.

claim: A hierarchical model was used to estimate the gametocyte density and its associated uncertainty at the same time as the age profile allowing the full uncertainty of the shape of the function to be expressed.
source_text: As above, a hierarchical model was used to estimate the gametocyte density and its associated uncertainty at the same time as the age profile allowing the full uncertainty of the shape of the function to be expressed
evidence_reasoning: This describes the statistical approach for analyzing the age profile.

claim: It is important to use individual host estimates of gametocyte density instead of mean estimates as the high degree of gametocyte overdispersion among hosts may accentuate the non-linear relationship between gametocyte density and mosquito infection.
source_text: It is important to use individual host estimates of gametocyte density instead of mean estimates as the high degree of gametocyte overdispersion among hosts may accentuate the non-linear relationship between gametocyte density and mosquito infection
evidence_reasoning: This is a methodological inference about the importance of accounting for overdispersion.

claim: For each of the 412 hosts, point estimates were obtained of the percentage of feeding mosquitoes that would develop oocysts according to the age and the gametocyte/asexual parasite density of the host.
source_text: For each of the 412 hosts, point estimates were obtained of the percentage of feeding mosquitoes (taking a single full blood meal) that would develop oocysts according to the age and the gametocyte/asexual parasite density of the host (equation 3)
evidence_reasoning: This describes the calculation performed for each individual in the survey.

claim: The best-fit line was used to predict the percentage of overall transmission that originated from hosts who had gametocyte density estimates below the detection threshold of microscopy.
source_text: This best-fit line was used to predict the percentage of overall transmission that originated from hosts who had gametocyte density estimates below the detection threshold of microscopy
evidence_reasoning: This describes an inference made from the fitted model.

claim: The detection threshold for microscopy is defined as the minimum (positive) density that can be estimated by sampling a certain volume of blood.
source_text: Here, we define the detection threshold as the minimum (positive) density that can be estimated by sampling a certain volume of blood
evidence_reasoning: This defines a technical term used in the analysis.

claim: It is assumed that gametocytes are counted against 500 white blood cells (WBC) and that there are on average 8000 WBC per µl of blood, giving an average detection threshold of 16 gametocytes per microlitre of blood.
source_text: It is assumed that gametocytes are counted against 500 white blood cells (WBC) and that there are on average 8000 WBC per µl of blood. This gives an average detection threshold of 16 gametocytes per microlitre of blood
evidence_reasoning: This describes standard assumptions for microscopy-based parasite counting.

claim: The 16 gametocytes per microlitre threshold is a conservative estimate since densities above this value may still give false negative results both due to reading errors or random sampling of gametocytes on the microscope slide.
source_text: This is a conservative estimate of the threshold density since densities above this value may still give false negative results both due reading errors or random sampling of gametocytes on the microscope slide
evidence_reasoning: This acknowledges limitations of microscopy that affect the threshold estimate.

claim: Care should be taken when interpreting the results as mosquito membrane feeding experiments were not performed with blood from adult hosts.
source_text: Care should be taken when interpreting the results as mosquito membrane feeding experiments were not performed with blood from adult hosts
evidence_reasoning: This acknowledges a limitation in the data collection.

claim: Evidence indicates that antibodies associated with transmission-blocking activity may be lower in older age groups.
source_text: Evidence indicates that antibodies associated with transmission-blocking activity may be lower in older age groups
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by reference to Drakeley et al., 2006.

claim: Adult hosts could have a greater potential to contribute to overall transmission than estimated in this study.
source_text: which could mean that adult hosts could have a greater potential to contribute to overall transmission
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about a potential bias in the estimates due to the lack of adult feeding assay data.

claim: Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo techniques were used to fit the models in OpenBUGS.
source_text: Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo techniques were used to fit the models in OpenBUGS
evidence_reasoning: This describes the statistical software and methods used.

claim: The Bayesian approach allows the uncertainties in the assessments of gametocyte density and mosquito infection rates to be taken into consideration and propagated into parameter posterior distributions.
source_text: This approach allows the uncertainties in the assessments of gametocyte density and mosquito infection rates (generated by different numbers of mosquitoes being dissected) to be taken into consideration, propagated into parameter posterior distributions
evidence_reasoning: This explains the advantage of the Bayesian statistical approach.

claim: All parameters were assigned uninformative priors.
source_text: All parameters were assigned uninformative priors
evidence_reasoning: This describes a feature of the Bayesian model specification.

claim: The most parsimonious models were selected by comparing deviance information criteria (DIC) values, with the lowest value giving the most parsimonious yet adequate fit.
source_text: The most parsimonious models were selected by comparing deviance information criteria (DIC) values (the lowest value giving the most parsimonious yet adequate fit)
evidence_reasoning: This describes the model selection criterion used.

claim: The distribution of gametocytes between hosts was highly overdispersed, with an aggregation parameter of the negative binomial distribution of 0.185 (95% Bayesian credible interval [CI], 0.16–0.21).
source_text: The distribution of gametocytes between hosts was highly overdispersed, with an aggregation parameter of the negative binomial distribution of 0.185 (95% Bayesian credible interval [CI], 0.16–0.21)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from the statistical analysis.
